A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MessIRve Spanish information-retrieval dataset. Their readable text, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, a human quality assessment of 650 query-document pairs, and analyses of topics and country-specific vocabulary.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical analyses and adds fine-tuning, cross-dataset retrieval evaluation, independent human and LLM assessments, and error analyses.

M1.justification: v2 introduces E5-large-ft-messirve, adapting the existing E5 model through fine-tuning with BM25-mined hard negatives (Section 5, Appendix A). v1 explicitly deferred fine-tuning to future work. This is a limited model adaptation; the core Google/Wikipedia collection approach and retrieval architecture are retained.

E1.justification: Retrieval evaluation expands from MessIRve alone to include MIRACL, mMARCO, SQAC, Multi-EuP and PRES (v2 Figure 4), adding parliamentary and health retrieval domains. These datasets were previously reviewed, and some underwent topic analysis, but v1 did not report retrieval evaluations on them.

E2.justification: The MessIRve comparison retains BM25, MIRACL-mdpr-es, E5-large and OpenAI-large, adding E5-large-ft-messirve as a fifth baseline. OpenAI-large is excluded from the newly introduced cross-dataset experiment for cost reasons, rather than removed from an existing comparison.

E3.justification: Tables 1–2 revise the reported full training/test counts from 571,120/160,099 to 537,730/156,528, with changes across country splits. v2 adds two-epoch fine-tuning, cross-dataset testing using MIRACL's development set and other datasets' test sets, and a three-rater assessment of 100 pairs plus LLM assessments of 650 pairs. The original author audit remains; the cause of the split revisions is unexplained.

E4.justification: v2 adds query-length and prefix-diversity analyses, a manual investigation of 30 retrieval failures, and examples diagnosing ambiguous queries and incorrect relevance judgments (Section 4.1, Section 5, Appendix B). It also examines Wikipedia editor representation. The earlier topic and country-vocabulary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B adds rating distributions and chance-adjusted Fleiss' kappa alongside percentage agreement, reporting 0.186, 0.146 and 0.089 for correctness, non-ambiguity and relevance. v2 explicitly acknowledges the absence of confidence intervals and significance testing. No repeated-run or seed reporting is introduced.

E6.justification: Full-set nDCG@10/Recall@100 change from 0.433/0.899 to 0.476/0.916 for OpenAI-large and from 0.430/0.847 to 0.463/0.865 for E5-large. Revised splits prevent interpreting these as gains under identical conditions. v2 adds fine-tuned E5 results of 0.491/0.887, cross-dataset rankings, and new quality and error-analysis findings; the original author-audit results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical contributions, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations. The added entropy and agreement statistics are empirical analysis tools, without new mathematical definitions or formal properties.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a large, naturally sourced Spanish retrieval dataset covering country variation. The introduction extends the stated contributions to cross-dataset evaluation and release of a fine-tuned baseline model. The abstract revises dataset size from around 730,000 to almost 700,000 queries.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of weak cross-dataset transfer, dataset-dependent lexical retrieval performance, and annotation problems behind retrieval failures. Appendix B qualifies raw agreement through class imbalance and low kappa. Expanded limitations discuss underrepresented communities, Wikipedia and Google biases, incomplete offensive-content screening, and missing statistical uncertainty estimates.

D1.justification: New Appendix A documents software versions, two 24GB A30 GPUs, training hyperparameters, token limits, frozen position embeddings and approximately 15 hours of training. Appendix C explains the existing autocomplete expansion procedure more precisely. v2 also supplies code and fine-tuned-model links and updates the dataset access location.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning RAG, annotation sparsity, AnCora, E5 training and implementation libraries, and replaces the BM25 reference to Robertson et al. (2009) with Robertson et al. (1994). The central positioning against the same five Spanish retrieval datasets remains.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of related work, dataset comparison and topic discussion are rewritten and condensed. v2 introduces a query-format subsection, consolidates the former experimental setup/results subsections, and reorganizes the single supporting appendix into Appendices A–C, including relocation of the original author audit.

P2.justification: v2 adds query-length boxplots, cross-dataset performance plots, prefix-entropy/count panels and a query-document example table. The MessIRve performance plot gains a fifth series and revised legend and captions. The original topic heatmap and Tables 3–5 are retained with renumbering or relocation.

improvement.justification: v1 relied on author-only quality assessment and left training utility and cross-dataset evaluation largely untested. v2 adds independent validation, demonstrates fine-tuning utility and transfer limitations, diagnoses annotation failures, and substantially improves reproducibility information. These strengthen the dataset's credibility and usefulness. The small independent audit, weak chance-adjusted agreement, absent confidence intervals and unexplained split/score revisions remain limitations.
